These 3 Maps Show the Disaster of the Venezuela Earthquakes

2026-07-02 Marshall Ritzel, AP News Venezuela earthquake, disaster mapping, seismic hazard, humanitarian mapping, Overture Maps, OpenStreetMap, building damage, displacement, crisis cartography
Read the source article

Quick summary

AP News used three data-driven maps to tell the story of two devastating earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, 2026 — killing over 2,200 people — combining seismic data, building footprints from Overture Maps, and displacement tracking to visualize a humanitarian catastrophe.

Key takeaways

  • Two earthquakes struck Venezuela on June 24, 2026, 39 seconds apart, killing more than 2,200 people by July 2
  • AP News published three complementary maps to tell the story: seismic intensity, building damage, and displacement patterns
  • Building footprint data from the Overture Maps Foundation was used to assess structural exposure and damage across affected areas
  • OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps data were combined in humanitarian datasets to fill gaps where OSM is sparse with machine-derived building footprints
  • Thousands of displaced people are sleeping in the open; the maps visualize the scale of displacement across affected regions
  • The project demonstrates how open geospatial data sources — OSM, Overture, and humanitarian datasets — enable rapid crisis cartography
  • Maps were published on the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX) for use by responders and researchers
